narrative: This is the Foresight intelligence briefing for the week of August 24th to August 30th. 167 developments crossed the priority threshold, 0 of them dated to this week as high-priority. The center of gravity is Justice & Rights, accounting for roughly 26 percent of what moved, with Climate & Environment close behind.

The lead story: European Commission Adopts First-Ever Strategy on Intergenerational Fairness, out of the international arena. This is the most significant institutional milestone for intergenerational fairness governance in the EU since the creation of the Commissioner portfolio itself. It sits on the present horizon.

Also demanding attention this week: South Africa’s Constitutional Court Restores Order Invalidating Wild Coast Oil and Gas Exploration Rights, in South Africa; and Montana Supreme Court Hears Oral Arguments on Attorney Fees and Agency Compliance in Held v. State, in the United States. The judgment operationalizes South Africa’s constitutional duty to protect the environment for present and future generations through concrete administrative-law remedies.
Reading the horizons: the week is over-indexing on present-day systems and institutions already in force, at 33 percent versus a 24 percent baseline.
